items.title: Local domain restriction for kick, drift, and leapfrog maps
A smooth local Hamiltonian flow preserves the canonical symplectic matrix
Local implicit midpoint step for a Hamiltonian vector field
Canonical kick and drift shears satisfy the symplectic Jacobian identity
Local leapfrog and kick-then-drift symplectic Euler are symplectic
Local and finite-time trajectory error for symplectic Euler and leapfrog
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, $V\in C^3(Q)$, and $M$ symmetric positive definite. Set $H(q,p)=\tfrac12p^TM^{-1}p+V(q)$ and $F(q,p)=(M^{-1}p,-\nabla V(q))$. Fix $T>0$ and $h=T/N$ with $N\ge1$. Suppose the exact solution, numerical states, all kick/drift intermediate states, and every line segment used below lie in one compact convex tube $K\Subset Q\times\mathbb R^d$, with the derivatives of $F$ through order two bounded there. For $z_0$ in that tube, write $e_n^E$ for the error of iterated kick-then-drift symplectic Euler and $e_n^V$ for the error of iterated local leapfrog relative to the exact solution at $t_n=nh$. Write $\Psi_h^E$ and $\Psi_h^V$ for their admitted one-step maps and $\varphi_h$ for the exact flow. For sufficiently small $h$, constants $C_E,C_V,L$ independent of $h,N,n$ satisfy
$$\|\Psi_h^E(z)-\varphi_h(z)\|\le C_Eh^2,\qquad \|\Psi_h^V(z)-\varphi_h(z)\|\le C_Vh^3$$
for admitted $z\in K$, and whenever $nh\le T$,
$$e_n^E\le e^{LT}e_0+C_ETe^{LT}h,\qquad e_n^V\le e^{LT}e_0+C_VTe^{LT}h^2.$$
Thus symplectic Euler has global order one and leapfrog has global order two on the stated controlled tube. No unconditional domain-admissibility claim is made.

items.title: The admitted implicit midpoint branch is symplectic and second order
A finite formal logarithm has Hamiltonian coefficients on a star-shaped domain
items.statement:
Let $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and star-shaped about a point $q_*\in Q$, meaning $q_*+t(q-q_*)\in Q$ for every $q\in Q$ and $t\in[0,1]$. Let $M$ be real symmetric positive-definite, $U=Q\times\mathbb R^d$, and equip $U$ with the canonical form $\omega=\sum_{i=1}^d dq_i\wedge dp_i$ and matrix $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I\\-I&0\end{pmatrix}$. Set $H(q,p)=\tfrac12p^TM^{-1}p+V(q)$ with $V\in C^\infty(Q)$. Let $\Phi_h$ be the kick-then-drift symplectic-Euler map, the local leapfrog map, or an admitted implicit-midpoint branch, on a compact subset where the chosen map is defined. Write $r=1$ for the kick-then-drift symplectic-Euler map and $r=2$ for leapfrog or implicit midpoint, as proved in [[thm-local-symplectic-euler-and-leapfrog-trajectory-errors]] and [[thm-implicit-midpoint-branch-symplectic-order-and-error]]. For a smooth test function $f$, define the pullback $P_hf=f\circ\Phi_h$ by its Taylor coefficients at $h=0$. For fixed finite $N\ge r$, its truncated logarithm is the polynomial
$$\log_N(P_h)=\sum_{k=1}^{N+1}\frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k}(P_h-I)^k,$$
computed modulo terms of order $h^{N+2}$. There are smooth vector fields $X_r,\ldots,X_N$ and globally defined functions $H_r,\ldots,H_N$ on $U$ such that
$$h^{-1}\log_N(P_h)=\mathcal L_{X_H}+\sum_{j=r}^Nh^j\mathcal L_{X_j}\pmod{h^{N+1}},\qquad \iota_{X_j}\omega=dH_j,$$
where $\mathcal L_Xf:=Df[X]$. Thus $H_h^{[N]}=H+\sum_{j=r}^Nh^jH_j$ is a globally defined finite modified Hamiltonian. The logarithm is a finite formal polynomial for each fixed $N$; no convergence of an infinite series is asserted.

items.title: A fixed finite modified flow matches its method map to the stated Taylor order
A fixed finite modified Hamiltonian is close to the original energy
The finite modified Hamiltonian has a bounded one-step defect
items.statement:
Fix $N\ge r$ and a compact comparison tube $K'\Subset U$. Let $H_h^{[N]}$ be the finite modified Hamiltonian from [[lem-finite-modified-hamiltonian-exists]]. Suppose $z$, $\Phi_h(z)$, the exact time-$h$ flow of $X_{H_h^{[N]}}$ from $z$, and the line segment joining those two endpoints all lie in $K'$. For sufficiently small $0<h\le1$, there is a constant $C_1$ independent of $z,h$ such that
$$|H_h^{[N]}(\Phi_h(z))-H_h^{[N]}(z)|\le C_1h^{N+1}.$$

items.title: Finite-order modified energy control on a compact tube
items.statement:
Let $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and star-shaped about a point $q_*\in Q$, meaning $q_*+t(q-q_*)\in Q$ for every $q\in Q$ and $t\in[0,1]$. Let $M$ be real symmetric positive-definite, $U=Q\times\mathbb R^d$, and $H(q,p)=\tfrac12p^TM^{-1}p+V(q)$ with $V\in C^\infty(Q)$. Choose one of this page's fixed-step methods: kick-then-drift symplectic Euler with $r=1$, or local leapfrog or an admitted implicit midpoint branch with $r=2$. Fix a finite truncation order $N\ge r$ and choose $h_0\in(0,1]$ small enough for the selected map and comparison flow branches. For one step size $0<h\le h_0$, let $z_{k+1}=\Phi_h(z_k)$ for $k=0,\ldots,n-1$, with $n\in\mathbb N_0$. Assume every numerical endpoint, every method stage, every truncated modified-flow comparison segment, and every segment used to compare $H$ with $H_h^{[N]}$ lies in one compact tube $K\Subset U$. Then there are constants $C_0,C_1$, independent of $h,n$, such that
$$|H(z_n)-H(z_0)|\le 2C_0h^r+C_1n h^{N+1}.$$
The bound holds only while the stated compact-tube and domain hypotheses hold; if $nh\le T$, its accumulated defect term is at most $C_1T h^N$. It asserts neither exact conservation of $H$ by the numerical method nor convergence of an infinite modified series.
